title: Peripheral artery disease: stage, side and ulcer
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's peripheral artery disease and any related ulcer.
note:
Chief Complaint: Calf pain when walking.

HPI: Pt is an 80-year-old female presenting for f/u of atherosclerotic changes. She reports persistent calf pain specifically when walking. She describes this as claudication. Pain is noted only in the right leg. She denies any pain while at rest. No skin breakdown or lesions present. Pt states symptoms have been consistent over the last few months.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg QD
- Atorvastatin 40mg QD
- Aspirin 81mg QD

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, weight change.
CV: Denies chest pain, palpitations, SOB.
MSK: Reports calf pain with exertion. No joint swelling.
Skin: Denies rashes or lesions.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

Social History: Retired. Lives in a single-story home with her daughter. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History: Mother had hypertension. Father had myocardial infarction at age 65.

Family History: Mother had hypertension. Father had myocardial infarction at age 65.

Vitals:
BP: 132/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Ht: 34%
Hgb: 11.2 g/dL
eGFR: 62

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears in no acute distress.
CV: RRR, regular rhythm. No murmurs.
Pulmonary: CTAB.
Extremities: Right lower extremity shows diminished pulses compared to left. Skin is intact. No edema. No visible lesions or skin breakdown noted.

Assessment:
1. Atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries with intermittent claudication. Symptoms localized to the right leg.

Plan:
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Instructed pt on supervised exercise program to improve walking distance.
3. Advised to monitor for any new skin changes or increased pain.
4. F/u in 3 months for progress.

Electronically signed,
T. Haddad, NP
05/14/2026
explanations: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the right leg with intermittent claudication (no HCC in V28): I70.211.

distractors.why: Rest pain is not documented (it would add HCC 264).
Atherosclerosis with claudication is documented: I70.21-.
